```python
def smallest_change(arr):
    """
    Given an array arr of integers, find the minimum number of elements that
    need to be changed to make the array palindromic. A palindromic array is an array that
    is read the same backwards and forwards. In one change, you can change one element to any other element.
    """
    start = 0
    end = len(arr) - 1
    change_count = 0

    while start <= end:

        # If both elements are the same, then move both pointers 
        if arr[start] == arr[end]:
            start += 1
            end -= 1

        # If elements are not same, then increment count of changes and also increment start pointer
        else:
            start += 1
            change_count += 1

    # return minimum change count
    return change_count
```

This function works by comparing the starting and ending elements of the array and then moving inwards. If the starting and ending elements don't match, one change is counted and the starting pointer is moved. If they do match, both pointers are moved without counting a change. The number of changes recorded by the time the pointers meet or cross each other is the number of changes needed to make the array palindromic.
